def-gr-fx-scalar-wave-stress:
## Definition

Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth
tangent-bundle conventions. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected
connection $\nabla$ and inverse metric $g^{ab}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open,
let $\psi\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ be a real scalar field, and let $X$ be a
smooth vector field on $U$. Define the wave operator
$\Box_g\psi:=g^{ab}\nabla_a\nabla_b\psi$ and the symmetric covariant tensor

$$Q_{ab}[\psi]:=(\nabla_a\psi)(\nabla_b\psi)-\frac12 g_{ab}g^{cd}(\nabla_c\psi)(\nabla_d\psi).$$

Define the multiplier covector by $J^X_a[\psi]:=Q_{ab}[\psi]X^b$. The
associated energy-current vector is $j_X^a[\psi]:=-g^{ab}J^X_b[\psi]$; this
sign convention makes its flux through a future spacelike slice equal to the
density $Q_{ab}n^aX^b$ when $n$ is the future unit normal. The test-wave
equation is $\Box_g\psi=0$ on $U$. These objects are defined on the fixed
background $g$; $Q$ is not automatically an SI matter stress-energy tensor,
is not inserted into an Einstein equation here, and does not evolve $g$.

If $\psi$ is dimensionless and the coordinates have length units, the
components of $Q$ have units of inverse length squared. This dimensional fact
does not identify $Q$ with a physical stress tensor without an independently
specified field normalization and coupling.
prop-gr-fx-wave-multiplier-identity:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold, let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let
$\psi\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$, and let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $U$.
For the tensor $Q_{ab}[\psi]$ and multiplier covector
$J_a^X[\psi]=Q_{ab}[\psi]X^b$ defined from the metric-selected connection,

$$\nabla^aJ_a^X[\psi]=(\Box_g\psi)\,X^b\nabla_b\psi+\frac12 Q^{ab}[\psi](\mathcal L_Xg)_{ab}.$$

Consequently, when $\Box_g\psi=0$ and $X$ is Killing, the multiplier current
has zero divergence.
lem-gr-fx-scalar-dominant-energy:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. At a point $p$ of a time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold, let $n$ be a future-directed unit timelike vector, let
$X\in T_pM$ be future causal, and let $\psi$ be a smooth real scalar. Put
$\ell:=\sharp_g(d\psi)$, $a:=d\psi(n)$,
$b:=h_n(\ell)\in n^\perp$, and $|b|^2:=g(b,b)$, where $h_n$ is the spatial
projection relative to $n$. Then

$$Q(n,n)=\frac12\bigl(a^2+|b|^2\bigr),\qquad Q(n,X)\geq0.$$
prop-gr-fx-schwarzschild-test-energy:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s>0$ and let $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ be the
regular advanced-chart extension of the Schwarzschild exterior, with
$f(r)=1-s/r$ and stationary field $T=\partial_v$. Let $C$ be a compact finite
smooth singular four-chain in the exterior closure $r\geq s$, with oriented
boundary
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+\mathcal H^++B_{\mathrm{out}}$, where
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$ are spacelike faces with future unit normals $n_1,n_2$,
$\mathcal H^+$ is a future-horizon face, and $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the
remaining signed outer boundary. Let $\psi$ be smooth on a neighborhood of
$C$ and solve $\Box_{g_{\mathrm{ext}}}\psi=0$. Define
$j_T^a:=-Q^{a}{}_{b}[\psi]T^b$. Orient each spacelike face $\Sigma_j$ so
that its adapted unit normal is the future unit normal $n_j$, and define

$$E_j:=\Phi_{j_T}(\Sigma_j)=\int_{\Sigma_j}Q_{ab}[\psi]n_j^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_j}.$$

Define $F_{\mathrm{out}}$ as the signed flux of
$j_T$ through $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ and
$F_H:=\int_{\mathcal H^+}(T\psi)^2\,d\mu_H$, where
$d\mu_H=s^2\,dv\,d\Omega$ is the positive horizon measure in the advanced
chart. Then $E_1,E_2,F_H\geq0$ and

$$E_2+F_H+F_{\mathrm{out}}=E_1.$$

The signed outer flux need not be nonnegative. On the exterior static slices
$x^0=\text{constant}$, $n=f^{-1/2}T$ and
$Q(n,T)=\sqrt f\,Q(n,n)$; this stationary slice energy degenerates as
$r\downarrow s$, where $T$ becomes null in the regular extension.
def-gr-fx-nondegenerate-local-energy-est:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior
datum with $s>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$, exterior coordinate $x^0$, and stationary
field $T=\partial_0$. Let $0<\delta<s/2$ and put
$K_\delta:=\{(x^0,r,\omega):|r-3s/2|\leq\delta\}$ for $\omega\in S^2$.
Then $K_\delta$ is contained in $r>s$. On the static slice
$\Sigma_{x^0}:=\{x^0=\text{constant}\}$ the future unit normal is
$n=f^{-1/2}T$. For a smooth real test wave $\psi$ with finite initial
stationary energy, define

$$E_T[\psi](x^0):=\int_{\Sigma_{x^0}}Q_{ab}[\psi]n^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{x^0}},\qquad E_{T,\delta}[\psi](x^0):=\int_{\Sigma_{x^0}\cap K_\delta}Q_{ab}[\psi]n^aT^b\,d\mu_{\Sigma_{x^0}}.$$

A **nondegenerate integrated local energy estimate with no trapping loss**
on $K_\delta$ means that there is a finite constant $C$, independent of
$\psi$, such that every smooth solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$ with finite
$E_T[\psi](0)$ satisfies

$$\int_0^\infty E_{T,\delta}[\psi](x^0)\,dx^0\leq C E_T[\psi](0).$$

Here “nondegenerate” means that the estimate integrates the full unweighted
first-derivative density, with no weight vanishing at $r=3s/2$; “no trapping
loss” means that the right side contains only the initial first-derivative
stationary energy, with no additional derivatives or degenerating weights.
This definition asserts no existence or nonexistence of such a constant.
def-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-mode:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M>0$, $0<|a|<M$, and use the length
coordinates of the subextremal Kerr datum. Let $H^+$ be a regular patch of
its future horizon, let $T$ and $\Phi$ be the stationary and axial Killing
fields, and let
$\chi:=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with
$\Omega_H:=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$ be the future null generator there. A smooth
complex scalar $u$ on a horizon patch is an $(\omega,m)$ **horizon mode**
when $\omega\in\mathbb R$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, and

$$Tu=-i\omega u,\qquad \Phi u=im u.$$

Its **shifted horizon frequency** is
$\widetilde\omega:=\omega-m\Omega_H$. By linearity of $\chi$, every such
mode satisfies $\chi u=-i\widetilde\omega u$. The parameter $\omega$ has
units reciprocal to the Kerr time coordinate, $m$ is dimensionless, and
$\Omega_H$ has the same units as $\omega$. This is a local definition of
mode data only; it does not assert that a nonzero mode extends to a global
solution of the wave equation.
lem-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-modal-flux:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $0<|a|<M$ and let $H^+$ be a regular
future Kerr horizon patch with stationary field $T$, axial field $\Phi$,
future null generator $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, and
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Let $u$ be a nonzero smooth $(\omega,m)$ mode
trace on $H^+$, where $\omega>0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, and suppose that
$\psi=\operatorname{Re}u$ is the trace of a smooth real scalar field near
$H^+$. No wave equation or global extension of the mode is assumed. Define
$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T$ as the average of the real scalar flux density
$Q_{ab}[\psi]\chi^aT^b$ over one stationary-flow period $2\pi/\omega$.
Then

$$\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T=\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)|u|^2.$$

Consequently, when $m\Omega_H>\omega>0$, this stationary horizon-flux density is nonpositive everywhere, is zero at every node $u=0$, and is strictly negative exactly where $u\ne0$.

For a compact smooth spacelike horizon-cut patch $D$ with nonempty interior and smooth boundary, contained in the mode domain, let $d\mu_D$ be the positive area measure of its induced metric. Define the integrated averaged stationary flux by
$$\mathcal F_D:=\int_D\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T\,d\mu_D =\frac12\omega(\omega-m\Omega_H)\int_D|u|^2\,d\mu_D.$$
In the same frequency band, $\mathcal F_D<0$ whenever $u|_D$ is not identically zero. A smooth nonzero mode therefore has strictly negative integrated averaged flux on a sufficiently small compact spacelike cut patch meeting its nonzero set. This is a conditional local mode-trace calculation; it does not assert the existence of a global wave or scattering solution.
lem-gr-fx-schwarzschild-gaussian-beam-co:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$, the stationary field $T=\partial_0$, and $0<\delta<s/2$. Let $K_\delta=\{|r-3s/2|\le\delta\}$ include the whole sphere factor, and use the stationary total and annular energies $E_T$ and $E_{T,\delta}$ defined for the real scalar test tensor. For every $H>0$ and every $0<\epsilon<1$, there is a real $\psi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2)$ solving $\Box_g\psi=0$, with compact smooth Cauchy data at $x^0=0$, such that

$$E_T[\psi](0)=1,\qquad E_{T,\delta}[\psi](x^0)\ge1-\epsilon\quad\text{for every }0\le x^0\le H.$$

The same solution works on the entire prescribed interval. Its stationary energy is finite and equal to one on every static slice. The frequency may depend on $H,\epsilon,s,\delta$; no infinite-time concentration, horizon extension, or concentration in a smaller angular neighborhood is asserted.
